In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of water vapour to the powdered soaps is a spontaneous process and is favoured by the addition of neutral salts, urea or sucrose.

the negative excess adsorption (or negative deviation) of water vapour from Raoult's law is due to the presence of the substrate and the negative deviation of the inorganic salts, sucrose or urea is due to the negative deviation of water vapour.
the adsorption of water on the surface of powdered soaps is a spontaneous process, which is facilitated in presence of salts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hydration of soaps and detergents is governed by a number of factors such as (i) hydrophobic and hydrophilic nature of the substrate, (ii) nature and size of the cation and (iii) nature of the anion of the inorganic salt and the neutral solute.
in presence of neutral salts and sucrose the standard free energy of binding of water vapour to soaps is more negative than that in absence of neutral salts and sugar.
the negative excess adsorption is more for inorganic salts than that for urea and sucroses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard free energy changes (delta G degrees ) of binding of urea, inorganic salt, and sucrose to the soaps have been found to be negative.
the hydration of long chain soaps is more than that of the corresponding detergents.
the standard free energy of binding water and neutral salts to soaps is always more negative than that of the corresponding detergents.
